QuestionText: Who is called the 'Father of the Nation' of India?
Explanation: Mahatma Gandhi is called the Father of the Nation. He led India's independence struggle through non-violence.

QuestionText: Who was the first Prime Minister of India?
Explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first Prime Minister, serving from 1947 until his death in 1964.

QuestionText: Who was India's first President?
Explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was India's first President, serving from 1950 to 1962.

QuestionText: Mahatma Gandhi was born on which date?
Explanation: Mahatma Gandhi was born on 2 October 1869. His birthday is celebrated as Gandhi Jayanti, a national holiday.

QuestionText: 'Netaji' is the title given to which freedom fighter?
Explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose was called 'Netaji' (Respected Leader). He formed the Indian National Army (INA).

QuestionText: Who gave the slogan 'Jai Hind'?
Explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose gave the famous slogan 'Jai Hind' (Victory to India). It became the rallying cry of the INA.

QuestionText: Who gave the slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad'?
Explanation: Bhagat Singh gave the slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad' (Long Live the Revolution). He was hanged at age 23.

QuestionText: Who is known as the 'Iron Man of India'?
Explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel is known as the Iron Man of India. He unified the 562 princely states into one nation.

QuestionText: Who was India's first woman Prime Minister?
Explanation: Indira Gandhi was India's first and only woman Prime Minister, serving from 1966–1977 and 1980–1984.

QuestionText: What was Mahatma Gandhi's real first name?
Explanation: Gandhi's full name was Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi. 'Mahatma' (Great Soul) was a title given by Rabindranath Tagore.

QuestionText: Who was called 'Lal-Bal-Pal' — which three leaders does this refer to?
Options: A) Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal
B) Lal Bahadur, Baldev Singh, Patel
C) Lala Amarnath, Bal Thackeray, Patel
Explanation: Lal-Bal-Pal refers to Lala Lajpat Rai (Lal), Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Bal), and Bipin Chandra Pal (Pal) — three aggressive nationalist leaders.

QuestionText: Who started the 'Dandi March' (Salt March) in 1930?
Explanation: Mahatma Gandhi started the Dandi March on 12 March 1930 to protest the British salt tax by making salt at Dandi, Gujarat.

QuestionText: Rabindranath Tagore was the first Asian to win which award?
Explanation: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for his collection 'Gitanjali'. He was the first Asian Nobel laureate.

QuestionText: Which scientist was known as the 'Missile Man of India'?
Explanation: Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam was called the 'Missile Man of India' for his work on missile development. He also served as India's 11th President.

QuestionText: Who is known as the 'Nightingale of India'?
Explanation: Sarojini Naidu was called the 'Nightingale of India' for her beautiful poetry. She was also the first Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress.

QuestionText: Who founded the Indian National Congress in 1885?
Explanation: The Indian National Congress was founded by A.O. Hume, a British civil servant, in 1885. It led India's freedom movement.

QuestionText: Who gave the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'?
Explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Lokmanya Tilak) gave this famous slogan, asserting Indians' right to self-governance.

QuestionText: Who is called the 'Grand Old Man of India'?
Explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji was called the 'Grand Old Man of India'. He was the first Indian to become a British MP and exposed the 'Drain Theory'.

QuestionText: Jawaharlal Nehru's birthday (14 November) is celebrated as which day?
Explanation: 14 November (Nehru's birthday) is celebrated as Children's Day (Bal Diwas) in India because of Nehru's love for children.

QuestionText: Who wrote the book 'The Discovery of India'?
Explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru wrote 'The Discovery of India' while imprisoned at Ahmadnagar Fort during 1942–46.

QuestionText: Which freedom fighter is associated with the slogan 'Do or Die'?
Explanation: Mahatma Gandhi gave the slogan 'Do or Die' (Karo ya Maro) during the Quit India Movement of 1942.

QuestionText: Who was the first woman to become President of the Indian National Congress?
Explanation: Annie Besant became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress in 1917.

QuestionText: Who discovered the 'Drain Theory' — that British rule drained India's wealth?
Explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji's 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901) detailed the Drain Theory — how Britain extracted India's wealth.

QuestionText: Who started the 'Home Rule League' movement in India?
Options: A) Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant
Explanation: Two Home Rule Leagues were started in 1916: one by Bal Gangadhar Tilak and another by Annie Besant.

QuestionText: What was the name of Mahatma Gandhi's autobiography?
Options: A) The Story of My Experiments with Truth
Explanation: Gandhi's autobiography is titled 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth', written in Gujarati.

QuestionText: Who wrote the book 'India Wins Freedom'?
Explanation: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad wrote 'India Wins Freedom', his autobiography that describes the independence movement and partition.

QuestionText: Dr. BR Ambedkar is known as the chief architect of which document?
Explanation: Dr. BR Ambedkar was the chairman of the Drafting Committee of India's Constitution and is called its chief architect.

QuestionText: Who was the first Deputy Prime Minister of India?
Explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel served as India's first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister.

QuestionText: Bhagat Singh was executed on which date?
Explanation: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev were hanged by the British on 23 March 1931 in Lahore. This day is observed as Shaheed Diwas.

QuestionText: Who founded the Arya Samaj, a Hindu reform movement?
Explanation: Swami Dayananda Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875 to reform Hinduism and fight social evils.

QuestionText: Who started the 'Brahmo Samaj' reform movement?
Explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828. He fought against sati, child marriage, and other social evils.

QuestionText: Who was called 'Punjab Kesari' (Lion of Punjab)?
Explanation: Lala Lajpat Rai was called 'Punjab Kesari'. He died from lathi blows received during a protest against the Simon Commission in 1928.

QuestionText: Who said 'Give me blood and I will give you freedom'?
Explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose gave this famous speech to motivate the Indian National Army soldiers to fight for independence.

QuestionText: Who was India's first woman IPS (police) officer?
Explanation: Kiran Bedi was India's first woman IPS officer, joining the service in 1972. She was also the first woman to head the UN civilian police.

QuestionText: Who is known as the 'Mother of the Indian Revolution'?
Explanation: Madam Bhikaji Cama is called the 'Mother of the Indian Revolution'. She unfurled an Indian flag at Stuttgart in 1907.

QuestionText: Which freedom fighter escaped from Alipore Jail and later became a spiritual leader?
Explanation: Sri Aurobindo (Aurobindo Ghose) was acquitted from Alipore Jail (1909) and later moved to Pondicherry, where he became a spiritual philosopher.

QuestionText: Who wrote 'Gitanjali', for which Tagore won the Nobel Prize?
Explanation: Rabindranath Tagore wrote 'Gitanjali' (Song Offerings) in Bengali. He translated it into English, and it won the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature.

QuestionText: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in which year?
Explanation: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on 13 April 1919 in Amritsar. General Dyer ordered troops to fire on a peaceful gathering.

QuestionText: Who was the last Viceroy of British India?
Explanation: Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy of British India. He oversaw the transfer of power and India's independence on 15 August 1947.

QuestionText: Which freedom fighter was known as 'Lokmanya' (respected by the people)?
Explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was called 'Lokmanya', meaning one respected by the people. He popularised the Ganesh Chaturthi festival as a national event.

QuestionText: Rani Lakshmibai was the queen of which kingdom?
Explanation: Rani Lakshmibai was the queen of Jhansi. She fought bravely against the British in the 1857 revolt and died in battle.

QuestionText: Who set up the Indian Independence League in Southeast Asia?
Explanation: Rash Behari Bose set up the Indian Independence League in Southeast Asia. He later handed its leadership to Subhas Chandra Bose.

QuestionText: Which Indian leader gave the concept of 'Swaraj' as complete self-rule?
Explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was the first to demand complete Swaraj (self-rule) as a political goal for India in clear terms.

QuestionText: Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated on which date?
Explanation: Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated on 30 January 1948 by Nathuram Godse. 30 January is observed as Martyrs' Day (Shaheed Diwas).

QuestionText: Who was the first woman Governor of an Indian state?
Explanation: Sarojini Naidu became the first woman Governor of an Indian state (United Provinces, now Uttar Pradesh) in 1947.

QuestionText: Which revolutionary threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly in 1929?
Options: A) Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt
B) Chandrashekhar Azad and Bhagat Singh
D) Ram Prasad Bismil and Ashfaqullah Khan
Explanation: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April 1929 to 'make the deaf hear'. The bomb was meant to make a statement, not kill.

QuestionText: Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam served as India's __ President.
Explanation: Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam served as India's 11th President from 2002 to 2007. He was a beloved scientist and educator.

QuestionText: Who was the first Indian to go to space?
Explanation: Rakesh Sharma was the first Indian to go to space in 1984 aboard the Soviet spacecraft Soyuz T-11.

QuestionText: Who was India's first female President?
Explanation: Pratibha Patil was India's first female President, serving from 2007 to 2012.

QuestionText: Swami Vivekananda's famous speech at the Parliament of World Religions was delivered in which city?
Explanation: Swami Vivekananda delivered his famous speech beginning 'Sisters and Brothers of America' at the Parliament of World Religions in Chicago in 1893.
